en: The Theravāda Vinaya:
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga,
Sekhiya Section
Parimaṇḍalavagga 1.
The Training Rule on Being Evenly Rounded.
Now, venerable ladies, these rules of training come up for recitation.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six bhikkhunīs were wearing their lower robes hanging down both in front and behind.
People complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can these bhikkhunīs wear their lower robes trailing both in front and behind, just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures?
The bhikkhunīs heard those people complaining, grumbling, and spreading it about.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [and so on]... complained, grumbled, and spread it about:
“How indeed can the group-of-six bhikkhunīs wear their lower robes trailing both in front and behind? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, bhikkhus, that the group-of-six bhikkhunīs wear their lower robes trailing both in front and behind?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunīs of the group of six wear their lower robes trailing both in front and behind?
This, bhikkhus, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith…” [and so on].
And furthermore, monks, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:
“The training is to be observed: ‘I shall put on the lower robe evenly all around.
It should be put on evenly all around, concealing the navel and the knees.
If, out of disrespect, she wears her lower robe hanging either in front or behind, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
through forgetfulness, through lack of knowledge,
or because she is ill;
In cases of misfortune,
for one who is insane,
or for one who is a first-time offender... [and so forth].
(Condensed.)
